title: Let there be light but not light pollution
content:
1. Less than 100 years ago, everyone could look up and see a beautiful night sky full of stars. Now, millions of children across the globe will never experience the Milky Way where they live. The increased and extensive use of artificial light at night not only destroys our view of the universe, it also has a negative effect on our environment, our safety, our energy consumption and our health.

2. Most of us are aware of air, water, and land pollution, but do you know that light can also be a pollutant?

3. The extensive use of artificial light – known as light pollution – can have serious environmental effects on humans, wildlife, and our climate. Factors that make up light pollution include:

4. • Glare – excessive brightness that causes discomfort to our vision

5. • Skyglow – brightening of the night sky over urban areas

6. • Light trespass – light falling where it is not intended or needed

7. • Clutter – bright, confusing and excessive combinations of light sources

8. Light pollution is a side effect of industrial civilization. Its sources include exterior and interior lighting from buildings, advertising, commercial properties, offices, factories, streetlights, and lighted sporting events.

9. The fact is that much outdoor lighting used at night is inefficient, too bright, poorly targeted, improperly shielded, and in many cases, completely unnecessary. This light, and the electricity used to create it, is being wasted when the light is projected into the sky, rather than onto the actual objects and areas that people want illuminated.

10. With much of the Earth's population living under light-polluted skies, over-lighting is an international concern. If you live in an urban or suburban area, all you have to do to see this type of pollution is go outside at night and look up at the sky.

11. According to the 2016 groundbreaking "World Atlas of Artificial Night Sky Brightness," 80 percent of the world's population lives under skyglow. As a result, in the United States and Europe 99 percent of the public can't experience a natural night!

12. For three billion years, life on Earth existed in a rhythm of light and dark that was created entirely by the illumination of the sun, the moon and stars. Now, artificial lights overpower the darkness and our cities shine at night, disrupting the natural day-night pattern and shifting the delicate balance of our environment. The negative effects of the loss of this natural resource might seem intangible. But a growing body of evidence links the brightening night sky directly to measurable negative impacts, including:

13. • Increasing energy consumption

14. • Disrupting the ecosystem and wildlife

15. • Harming human health

16. • Effecting crime and safety

17. Light pollution affects every citizen. Fortunately, concern about light pollution is rising significantly. A growing number of scientists, homeowners, environmental groups and civic leaders are taking action to restore the natural night. Each of us can carry out practical solutions to combat light pollution locally, nationally and internationally.
